# Khemātherīgāthā (Thig 6.3)

**ID:** Thig 6.3
**Section:** Therīgāthā (thig)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Khemātherīgāthā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0509m.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khemātherīgāthā* (Thig 6.3) is a six-verse poem in the *Therīgāthā* attributed to the elder nun Khemā, who is traditionally recognized as the Buddha's foremost female disciple in wisdom [Emmanuel 2013_A]. The poem is framed as a dialogue in verse in which Khemā confronts and rejects the advances of a young seducer who praises her physical beauty [Cheng 2007; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. While the verses in the *Therīgāthā* can read as a dialogue between lovers, the commentary explains that the youth was actually Māra attempting to divert her from her spiritual attainment [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Collett 2014]. In her response, Khemā rejects attachment to the impermanent body, physical beauty, and sensual pleasures, declaring her liberation from suffering and lust [Cheng 2007; Nyanaponika et al. 2003].
